sections.skill: Choose a filing method, meet deadlines, and avoid tax scams

questions.prompt: When are federal individual income tax returns generally due?

choices.text: April 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday)

questions.correct_answer: April 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday)
questions.intro: Federal returns for a calendar year are generally due April 15 of the following year. If that day falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.
questions.feedback: Returns are generally due April 15 (or the next business day).
questions.topic: Filing a return: methods, deadlines, and scams
sources: IRS: Individual returns are generally due April 15 (next business day if on a weekend or holiday); an extension extends the time to file, not to pay; IRS Free File and VITA offer free filing help to eligible taxpayers. (https://www.irs.gov/filing)
IRS (Tax scams): The IRS does not demand immediate payment by gift card, wire, or cryptocurrency, or threaten arrest by phone. (https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/tax-scams-consumer-alerts)

questions.prompt: Kayla, a student with simple taxes, wants to file for free. Which options may be available?

choices.text: IRS Free File or a VITA free tax help site
Filing through a social media influencer's link
Mailing her W-2 to her employer

questions.correct_answer: IRS Free File or a VITA free tax help site
questions.intro: Ways to file: tax software (including IRS Free File for eligible incomes), free in-person help through VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) for eligible taxpayers, a paid preparer, or paper forms. E-filing with direct deposit gets refunds fastest.
questions.feedback: IRS Free File and VITA offer free filing for many taxpayers.

questions.prompt: A caller says he is from the IRS and that Kayla will be arrested unless she pays $900 today with gift cards. What should she do?

choices.text: Buy the gift cards to avoid arrest
Give her Social Security number to verify
Pay half now to show good faith
Hang up; the IRS does not demand gift-card payment or threaten arrest by phone

questions.correct_answer: Hang up; the IRS does not demand gift-card payment or threaten arrest by phone
questions.intro: IRS impersonation scams are common. The IRS generally contacts people first by mail, never demands immediate payment by gift card, wire, or cryptocurrency, and does not threaten arrest by phone.
questions.feedback: Threats and gift-card demands are signs of an IRS scam.

questions.prompt: Kayla files for a 6-month extension. What new deadline does she have, and what is NOT extended?

choices.text: About October 15 to file and to pay

questions.correct_answer: About October 15 to file; payment of any tax owed is not extended
questions.intro: An automatic extension (Form 4868) moves the filing deadline about six months, generally to October 15, but tax owed is still due in April.
questions.feedback: The extension covers filing only; payment is still due in April.

questions.prompt: A thief files a return using Kayla's Social Security number to steal her refund. What is this called?

choices.text: A tax credit claimed by mistake

questions.intro: In tax-related identity theft, someone uses your Social Security number to file a fraudulent return and claim a refund. Filing early and using an IRS Identity Protection PIN help prevent it.
questions.feedback: Using someone's SSN to file is tax identity theft.

questions.prompt: What does an IRS Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN) do?

choices.text: It must be entered on the return, blocking others from filing with your SSN
It replaces your Social Security number
It speeds up refunds to any account

questions.correct_answer: It must be entered on the return, blocking others from filing with your SSN
questions.intro: An IP PIN is a six-digit number known only to you and the IRS that must appear on your return.
questions.feedback: Returns filed without your IP PIN are rejected, preventing fraud.
